title: tvbuff: support endianness setting for packed bcd
description:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary-coded_decimal says about packed BCD:
"Most implementations are big endian, ..."

However, the ENC_BCD_DIGITS_0_9 encoding for packed BCD values is
hard-wired to little endian for mulit-byte fields.

Some dissectors like zvt work around this by calling tvb_get_bcd_string
and proto_tree_add_string.

This patch allows setting ENC_BIG_ENDIAN or ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN in
combination with ENC_BCD_DIGITS_0_9. Unfortunately, we have to default to
big endian and fix up all existing users.

notes.body:
I noticed this when I looked at some fields in the MDB protocol which are big endian packed BCD.

Please let me know if I missed some use cases or if I misunderstood things.

Hi,

did you close this by mistake?

If not, could you give me some hints what could be improved to make this change acceptable?

Thanks,
Martin
Sorry yes I must have closed it by mistake.
Shouldn't all calls to tvb_get_bcd_string() inside of tvb_get_string_enc() have the same behaviour?

The other callers of tvb_get_bcd_string are ENC_KEYPAD_ABC_TBCD and ENC_KEYPAD_BC_TBCD. To me, it looks like these encodings are specific to some telephony protocols who happen to be little endian.

I doubt that there will be any users for these encodings in big endian. There's nobody who calls tvb_get_bcd_string with Dgt_keypad_abc_tbcd or Dgt_ansi_tbcd to extract bcd numbers in big endian.

> There's nobody who calls tvb_get_bcd_string with Dgt_keypad_abc_tbcd or Dgt_ansi_tbcd to extract bcd numbers in big endian.

There's no dissector that directly calls `tvb_get_bcd_string()` with `Dgt_keypad_abc_tbcd` or `Dgt_ansi_tbcd` *at all*; the only direct calls are from dissectors using their own private versions of `Dgt0_9_bcd` (before some recent changes I made, some private versions were mistakenly named `Dgt1_9_bcd` even though they supported 0) to extract BCD numbers in big-endian.

Once this change is committed, those calls can be replaced with calls using `ENC_BCD_DIGITS_0_9|ENC_BIG_ENDIAN` as the encoding, and `tvb_get_bcd_string()` could be made static.
And supporting `ENC_BIG_ENDIAN` and `ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN` for *all* BCD encodings is a bit cleaner - no special cases (even if those special cases don't turn up).
Ok, that's a good point. It makes sense to treat all BCD variants in the same way. I'll update the patch accordingly.
I've just uploaded a version that checks endianness for all bcd encodings.

> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binary-coded_decimal says about packed BCD: "Most implementations are big endian, ..."

To be fair, it says that in a section that's mostly talking about the storage of digits in computer memory in programs, rather than in communications protocols - and they may be thinking only of machines with packed decimal arithmetic instructions, where a lot of them are S/3x0 machines, which are big-endian.  (And Wireshark can run on S/390 and z/Architecture machines, as long as they're running an OS on which Wireshark is supported....)

In protocols (the implementations of which probably run on machines with little or no native packed BCD support), little-endian may be more common.

But, yes, as long as both encodings are used in protocols, we should support both.
Thanks for the clarification.

commits_data.title: tvbuff: support endianness setting for packed BCD
commits_data.message:
tvbuff: support endianness setting for packed BCD

ENC_BCD_DIGITS_0_9 and other encodings for packed BCD values are
hard-wired to little endian for multi-byte fields.

Some dissectors like zvt work around this by calling tvb_get_bcd_string
and proto_tree_add_string. The mdb protocol is also using multi-byte
packed BCD fields in big-endian order.

This patch allows setting ENC_BIG_ENDIAN or ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN in
combination with the BCD encodings. Unfortunately, we have to default to
big endian and fix up all existing users.
